export const meta = { name: "sbps-parallel-impl", description: "Implement site-based buyer matching and contact discovery in parallel", phases: [{ title: "build", description: "Both tracks in parallel" }] };

const trackA = agent({
  prompt: `You are implementing site-based buyer demand matching for the SBPS Supply Radar, a Python 3.11 project at /home/alex/Projects/SBPS.

## Context
The radar discovers surplus power equipment from public signals. Currently buyers only match on equipment type/capacity/frequency/voltage. A new buyer type needs to match on SITES — land with connected power infrastructure (e.g., "Need land with Power 50-100+MW, former data center or mining center or papermill, permitted for commercial use").

## Your tasks — make ALL changes directly:

### 1. Extend models (src/sbps/models.py)
a) New enums after Frequency:
- DemandType(StrEnum): EQUIPMENT = "equipment", SITE_WITH_POWER = "site_with_power"
- SiteType(StrEnum): DATA_CENTER = "data_center", PAPER_MILL = "paper_mill", MINING = "mining", UTILITY_PLANT = "utility_plant", INDUSTRIAL = "industrial", FARM_LAND = "farm_land", UNKNOWN = "unknown"
- DealStructure(StrEnum): JV = "jv", PURCHASE = "purchase", LEASE = "lease", UNKNOWN = "unknown"

b) Add to Signal model after is_new_surplus:
    site_type: SiteType = SiteType.UNKNOWN
    interconnection_mw: float | None = None
    acreage: float | None = None
    permitting_status: str = ""

c) Add to BuyerDemand after priority:
    demand_type: DemandType = DemandType.EQUIPMENT
    site_type_preference: list[SiteType] = Field(default_factory=list)
    permitting_requirement: str = ""
    deal_structure: DealStructure = DealStructure.UNKNOWN

### 2. Update enricher (src/sbps/enricher.py)
- Import SiteType
- Add site_type, interconnection_mw, acreage, permitting_status to ENRICH_PROMPT JSON schema
- Parse these fields in enrich() after is_new_surplus parsing
- Add site_type to log line

### 3. Update buyer_matcher (src/sbps/buyer_matcher.py)
- Import DemandType, SiteType
- Parse new CSV fields in load_buyers
- Add _site_type_matches() and _is_site_becoming_available() functions
- Replace match_buyers to handle both demand types (EQUIPMENT = existing behavior, SITE_WITH_POWER = site type + capacity + availability check)

### 4. Update data/buyers.csv.example
Add columns: demand_type,site_type_preference,permitting_requirement,deal_structure
Add buyer b006: JV Data Center Developer, site_with_power, data_center|mining|paper_mill|utility_plant|farm_land, commercial-permitted, jv, 50-100MW

### 5. Update tests (tests/test_buyer_matcher.py)
Add tests for: _site_type_matches, _is_site_becoming_available, site buyer matching retirement signal, site buyer no match wrong type, site buyer no match no availability, equipment buyer unchanged (regression)

IMPORTANT: Read each file before editing. Use ctx_edit for all edits. After all edits, run: cd /home/alex/Projects/SBPS && python -m pytest tests/test_buyer_matcher.py -v 2>&1 | tail -30`
});

const trackB = agent({
  prompt: `You are implementing a contact point-person discovery module for the SBPS Supply Radar, a Python 3.11 project at /home/alex/Projects/SBPS.

## Context
The radar discovers surplus power equipment and identifies the company that owns it. The critical gap: there's no mechanism to identify the specific HUMAN at that company who handles asset disposition. The system needs to infer likely role titles from the trigger event and query people-data APIs.

## Your tasks — make ALL changes directly:

### 1. Add config field (src/sbps/config.py)
Add after recap_api_token:
    apollo_api_key: str = field(default_factory=lambda: os.getenv("APOLLO_API_KEY", ""))

### 2. Create src/sbps/contact_discovery.py
Full module with:
- TRIGGER_ROLE_MAP dict: keywords (bankrupt, chapter, retire, decommission, cancel, withdraw, dismiss, impair, sell, surplus, close, shut down) to role title lists
- DEFAULT_ROLES list: Asset Disposition Manager, Director of Asset Management, Plant Manager, VP Operations, CFO
- SOURCE_ROLE_HINTS dict: SignalSource to role lists (PACER to CRO/CFO/GC, EIA_RETIREMENT to Plant Manager/Asset Mgmt, etc.)
- ContactCandidate dataclass: name, title, company, email, phone, linkedin_url, confidence, source, outreach_angle
- DiscoveryResult dataclass: signal_id, company_name, inferred_roles, candidates, best_candidate, outreach_strategy
- infer_roles(signal) -> list[str]: match trigger keywords, fall back to source hints, then defaults
- build_outreach_angle(signal, role_title="") -> str: trigger-specific messaging. Bankruptcy to speed/certainty. Retirement to before demolition. Cancellation to idle equipment. Impairment to balance sheet relief. Generic to SBPS transparent 1/1/1 differentiator. Always include company name.
- search_apollo(company_name, role_titles, api_key) -> list[ContactCandidate]: POST to https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/people/search with X-Api-Key header, search top 3 roles, 5 per page. Return [] if no key.
- rank_candidates(candidates, preferred_roles) -> sorted list by role match quality
- ContactDiscovery class: discover(signal) and discover_batch(signals). Without API key, create inferred placeholders (empty name, source="inferred").

### 3. Integrate with call sheet (src/sbps/call_sheet.py)
Replace _build_suggested_angle to delegate to contact_discovery.build_outreach_angle(signal, "")

### 4. Integrate into CLI (src/sbps/cli.py)
Add import ContactDiscovery. In _run_pipeline, after step 6 (buyer matching), add step 6b: discover contacts.

### 5. Write tests (tests/test_contact_discovery.py)
Test infer_roles (retirement/bankruptcy/cancellation/unknown/source hints), build_outreach_angle (bankruptcy/retirement/generic), rank_candidates, ContactDiscovery.discover (no API key, empty company), discover_batch. Use pytest.mark.asyncio.

### 6. Ensure pytest-asyncio available
Read pyproject.toml. If pytest-asyncio not in dev deps, add it. Add asyncio_mode="auto" to pytest config if missing.

IMPORTANT: Read each file before editing. Use ctx_edit for all edits. After all edits, run: cd /home/alex/Projects/SBPS && python -m pytest tests/test_contact_discovery.py -v 2>&1 | tail -40`
});

return Promise.all([trackA, trackB]);

"""Tests for the buyer matcher."""

from sbps.models import (
    BuyerDemand,
    EquipmentType,
    Frequency,
    Signal,
    SignalSource,
)
from sbps.buyer_matcher import (
    match_buyers,
    match_signals_to_buyers,
    _capacity_matches,
    _equipment_type_matches,
    _frequency_matches,
)


def _make_signal(**kwargs) -> Signal:
    defaults = dict(
        id="test_1",
        source=SignalSource.EIA_RETIREMENT,
        raw_text="test",
        is_equipment_related=True,
        confidence_score=0.8,
        equipment_types=[EquipmentType.GAS_TURBINE],
        capacity_mw=250,
        frequency=Frequency.HZ_60,
    )
    defaults.update(kwargs)
    return Signal(**defaults)


def _make_buyer(**kwargs) -> BuyerDemand:
    defaults = dict(
        buyer_id="buyer_1",
        buyer_name="Test Buyer",
        equipment_types=[EquipmentType.GAS_TURBINE],
        capacity_range_mw=(100, 500),
        frequency=Frequency.HZ_60,
        priority=0.8,
    )
    defaults.update(kwargs)
    return BuyerDemand(**defaults)


def test_frequency_hard_gate():
    """50Hz equipment should NOT match a 60Hz buyer."""
    assert _frequency_matches(Frequency.HZ_50, Frequency.HZ_60) is False
    assert _frequency_matches(Frequency.HZ_60, Frequency.HZ_60) is True
    assert _frequency_matches(Frequency.HZ_50, Frequency.UNKNOWN) is True
    assert _frequency_matches(Frequency.UNKNOWN, Frequency.HZ_60) is True


def test_capacity_range():
    """Capacity should fall within buyer's range."""

    assert _capacity_matches(50, (100, 500)) is False
    assert _capacity_matches(600, (100, 500)) is False
    assert _capacity_matches(None, (100, 500)) is True  # Unknown = don't filter

You are implementing a contact point-person discovery module for the SBPS Supply Radar, a Python 3.11 project at /home/alex/Projects/SBPS.

## Context
The radar discovers surplus power equipment and identifies the company that owns it. The critical gap: there's no mechanism to identify the specific HUMAN at that company who handles asset disposition. The system needs to infer likely role titles from the trigger event and query people-data APIs.

## Your tasks — make ALL changes directly:

### 1. Add config field (src/sbps/config.py)
Add after recap_api_token:
    apollo_api_key: str = field(default_factory=lambda: os.getenv("APOLLO_API_KEY", ""))

### 2. Create src/sbps/contact_discovery.py
Full module with:
- TRIGGER_ROLE_MAP dict: keywords (bankrupt, chapter, retire, decommission, cancel, withdraw, dismiss, impair, sell, surplus, close, shut down) to role title lists
- DEFAULT_ROLES list: Asset Disposition Manager, Director of Asset Management, Plant Manager, VP Operations, CFO
- SOURCE_ROLE_HINTS dict: SignalSource to role lists (PACER to CRO/CFO/GC, EIA_RETIREMENT to Plant Manager/Asset Mgmt, etc.)
- ContactCandidate dataclass: name, title, company, email, phone, linkedin_url, confidence, source, outreach_angle
- DiscoveryResult dataclass: signal_id, company_name, inferred_roles, candidates, best_candidate, outreach_strategy
- infer_roles(signal) -> list[str]: match trigger keywords, fall back to source hints, then defaults
- build_outreach_angle(signal, role_title="") -> str: trigger-specific messaging. Bankruptcy to speed/certainty. Retirement to before demolition. Cancellation to idle equipment. Impairment to balance sheet relief. Generic to SBPS transparent 1/1/1 differentiator. Always include company name.
- search_apollo(company_name, role_titles, api_key) -> list[ContactCandidate]: POST to https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/people/search with X-Api-Key header, search top 3 roles, 5 per page. Return [] if no key.
- rank_candidates(candidates, preferred_roles) -> sorted list by role match quality
- ContactDiscovery class: discover(signal) and discover_batch(signals). Without API key, create inferred placeholders (empty name, source="inferred").

### 3. Integrate with call sheet (src/sbps/call_sheet.py)
Replace _build_suggested_angle to delegate to contact_discovery.build_outreach_angle(signal, "")

### 4. Integrate into CLI (src/sbps/cli.py)
Add import ContactDiscovery. In _run_pipeline, after step 6 (buyer matching), add step 6b: discover contacts.

### 5. Write tests (tests/test_contact_discovery.py)
Test infer_roles (retirement/bankruptcy/cancellation/unknown/source hints), build_outreach_angle (bankruptcy/retirement/generic), rank_candidates, ContactDiscovery.discover (no API key, empty company), discover_batch. Use pytest.mark.asyncio.

### 6. Ensure pytest-asyncio available
Read pyproject.toml. If pytest-asyncio not in dev deps, add it. Add asyncio_mode="auto" to pytest config if missing.
